snapshot.capital_bootstrap: ₹5–15 lakh for a small shop or a packaged range
snapshot.capital_scaled: ₹40 lakh–1.5 crore for a larger shop with a kitchen and gifting business
snapshot.margin_d2c: 50–65% gross margin on sweets sold at the counter
snapshot.margin_production: 25–35% through retail, corporate gifting and marketplaces
snapshot.distribution_note: Festivals and gifting bring most sales; location and reputation do the rest

tailwinds: Festivals such as Diwali, Raksha Bandhan and weddings bring huge demand every year.
Corporate gifting and premium boxed sweets are growing fast.
Sugar-free, millet and healthier sweets appeal to a new group of buyers.
Online and quick-commerce sales let sweet brands reach beyond their neighbourhood.
headwinds: Most traditional sweets have a very short shelf life.
Milk, ghee and dry-fruit prices keep rising.
Food safety inspections are strict around festivals, and adulteration scandals hurt trust.
Established shops have decades of goodwill.
angle_2026: Sweet buyers are split: some want traditional mithai from a trusted shop, others want premium, healthier or modern confectionery. In 2026, new sweet businesses do well by picking one side, such as premium gifting, sugar-free, or long-shelf-life packaged sweets, rather than competing with the neighbourhood halwai.
cost_basis: Estimated for a small sweet shop or packaged sweets brand with its own kitchen, 2026 prices.

setup_costs.covers: Milk, ghee, sugar, dry fruits, packaging
FSSAI licence, trade licence, lab tests

bootstrap_takeaway: Start with a small range of your best sweets, sell through festival pre-orders and corporate gifting, and open a shop only when you have steady demand.
sourcing_edge: Buying milk directly from dairies and dry fruits from wholesale markets such as Delhi's Khari Baoli cuts costs.
licences: Trade licence or health licence from the municipality
Legal Metrology labelling for packaged sweets, including the 'best before' date

hard_truths.title: Short shelf life
hard_truths.text: Milk sweets spoil within days. Make to order and plan stock carefully.

hard_truths.title: Festival crunch
hard_truths.text: You'll be overwhelmed at Diwali and quiet at other times. Hire temporary staff and plan cash flow.

hard_truths.title: Food safety
hard_truths.text: One case of adulteration or illness can ruin your reputation. Test ingredients and keep records.

hard_truths.title: Rising costs
hard_truths.text: Milk and ghee prices rise every year. Review prices regularly.

plan_goal: The aim is ₹2 lakh in sales, including one festival or corporate order.

steps: Get your FSSAI licence and set up a kitchen.
